key_insight: Bayesian inference fused with photoluminescence imaging and drift-diffusion modeling can localize perovskite solar-cell degradation to specific interfaces or the bulk over time.
engineering_relevance: The method helps engineers diagnose failure mechanisms in aged perovskite devices and guides targeted stability improvements such as interface passivation.
method: Photoluminescence imaging of fully fabricated perovskite solar cells
Drift-diffusion simulations linked to measured optoelectronic behavior
Bayesian inference to produce spatially resolved parameter maps during aging
evidence_signal: Under 70 °C full-spectrum sunlight aging, the inferred maps showed pronounced spatial heterogeneity and identified the strongest degradation in perovskite/transport-layer interfacial regions, which was reduced by amino-silane passivation.
watch_item: The approach depends on model assumptions and high-quality imaging/simulation alignment, so inferred degradation locations should be validated against independent physical measurements.
paper_title: Disentangling the origin of degradation in perovskite solar cells via optical imaging and Bayesian inference
